sources.title: Scientific References
sources.pomodoroDesc: Original 25/5 pattern with 4-cycle structure. Foundation of structured interval-based focus.
sources.desktimeDesc: Analysis of top 10% most productive workers found 52/17 work-break ratio. Updated data suggests 75–112 min sessions.
sources.ultradianDesc: 90–120 minute biological rhythm affecting alertness and cognitive performance during wakefulness.
sources.hubermanDesc: Neurobiological basis for 90-minute focus sessions with 10–30 min defocus periods. Max 2–3 sessions per day.
sources.microbreaksDesc: Systematic review showing longer breaks yield greater performance recovery, especially after depleting tasks.
sources.breakRatioDesc: Most productive people spend 20–25% of their workday on breaks. Break quality matters as much as duration.

datenschutz.title: Privacy notice
datenschutz.private: pgoell.com is a private, non-commercial website. There is no data protection officer, and the law does not require one.

sections.title: 2. What this website is
text: pgoell.com shows writing, small games and tools. There are no user accounts, no contact form and no comments. There are no analytics or tracking tools and no ads.
If you send me an email, I use what you write only to answer you (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Cloudflare receives the email and forwards it to my mailbox (see section 7).

sections.title: 3. Visiting the website
text: Each time you open a page, the server handles the data it needs to answer: IP address, date and time, the address you asked for and your browser's user agent. Without this data it cannot send the page. The server keeps no access log.
Server error messages may contain the IP address. I use them only to find faults and keep the server safe. I do not use them to identify people and do not combine them with other data.
The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to deliver the site safely and without faults.

sections.title: 4. Cookies
text: The website sets one cookie named "NEXT_LOCALE". It remembers the language you chose and expires after one year. It is technically necessary and needs no consent under § 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG.

The trip pages have a sign-in for people I have invited. You sign in with your Google account. Google (Google Ireland Limited, with Google LLC, USA, certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework) runs the sign-in, sees your IP address while you sign in and sends this website your basic profile. The website uses your email address to check that you are invited and your first name to show who added a place or an idea (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Two cookies then hold the sign-in: "trips_session" holds your name and email address, signed so that nobody can change them; "trips_signed_in" holds only the number 1, so the pages know to load the private trips; both last 90 days or until you sign out. While you sign in, two more cookies guard the sign-in itself and the page to come back to; they last ten minutes. All four are technically necessary for the sign-in (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG).

The places, ideas and notes that signed-in people enter sit in a database on this website's server, each place and idea with the first name of who added it. On a trip open to all, anyone can see the route, the places and the day notes; bookings and ideas stay behind the sign-in. Entries stay until someone on the trip deletes them, or until you ask me to. The server backs up the database at most once an hour and keeps the newest 48 copies; once a night a copy also goes to a storage box rented from Hetzner, kept for up to a year.

sections.title: 5. Storage in your browser
text: Some pages keep data in your browser's local storage (localStorage): the colour theme you chose, the game state and keyboard setting of Wordle, the keyboard setting of the Wordle solver, the game state of Kniffel, the state and statistics of the Pomodoro timer, and the Night or Day look of the trip pages.

For people signed in to the trip pages, the browser also keeps a copy of the trip pages they open, their scripts and styles, and the map parts they have seen, so a trip still opens without a network (a service worker with its cache storage). The copy holds what a signed-in person sees, bookings included, stays on the device and is never sent anywhere. It stays until you clear the site's data in your browser.
This data stays on your device and never goes to the server. The feature you open needs it to work (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG). You can delete it at any time in your browser settings.

sections.title: 6. Hosting
text: The website runs on a server of Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany, in a data centre in Germany. A data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR is in place with Hetzner.

sections.title: 7. Cloudflare
text: All requests to pgoell.com pass through the network of Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. Cloudflare forwards the requests to the server, shields it from attacks and encrypts the connection. In doing so, Cloudflare handles the connection data named in section 3. If a connection fails, your browser may send an error report to Cloudflare.
Cloudflare also hides email addresses in the page text from spam robots and adds a small script to do so. The script comes from pgoell.com and stores nothing on your device.

Cloudflare is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, so a transfer to the USA is allowed under Art. 45 GDPR. A data processing agreement is in place with Cloudflare. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to keep the site safe and reachable.

sections.title: 8. Fonts and external content
text: For visitors, the website loads no fonts, scripts or images from other servers. References to other websites, such as GitHub, LinkedIn and X, are plain links. The other site learns of you only when you click the link.
For people signed in to the trip pages, a few things do reach other servers. They are part of what the trip pages do for invited people (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR):

Google Maps: when you open a place, its place card and place search load from Google Maps (Google Ireland Limited, with Google LLC, USA, certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework). Google then sees your IP address and which place you look at. The website keeps only Google's ID for the place. If you are not signed in, your browser never contacts Google Maps.

Routes: if you draw a route along roads, the server sends the route's points to the public router at router.project-osrm.org to find the roads. The request comes from the server, not from your browser, so the router does not learn who you are.

Satellite images: if you switch the map to satellite images, the server fetches them from Esri (Environmental Systems Research Institute, USA) and passes them on. Esri sees which part of the map is asked for, from the server, not from your browser.
Links: if you save a link to a place, the server opens that page once to read its title and location. The other site sees a request from the server, not from you.
Your position: "Near me" and the map's location button read your position only while they are switched on. The position stays in your browser and never reaches the server.

sections.title: 9. Your rights
text: You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), to rectification (Art. 16), to erasure (Art. 17), to restriction of processing (Art. 18), to data portability (Art. 20) and to object to processing based on Art. 6(1)(f) (Art. 21). An email to the address above is enough.

You can also complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example Der Hessische Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit, Postfach 3163, 65021 Wiesbaden, Germany, datenschutz.hessen.de.

sections.title: 10. Changes
text: Before the website does anything new with data, I will update this notice.
